body:
soy@beans.gm (Not Bagehot) wrote:

>Nobody should be exempt from criticism, particularly the kind of
>people who would readily agree with the Unabomber that '[t]he
>Industrial Revolution and its consequences have been a disaster for
>the human race.' 

Criticism, of the truly constructive kind (which, imo, is a skill that many
people have yet to master) is certainly valuable, even moreso in the form of
engaging true debate. Which, of course has been pointed out here before.

As far as those who would agree that "the Industrial Revolution and its
consequences have been a disaster for the human race," most of them may not
even be aware of TK's views. Take a break with people at work, and bring up one
of the topics in ISAIF, without revealing the source, and note the reaction.  I
do not believe in blanketly agreeing with someone because you were impressed by
their prose. And, I do not believe in dismissing something out of hand, because
of bad PR. Truth can be found in curious places. And, you do have to be curious
enough to get beyond the surface to find it. 

-Susan
